outputs.headline: False: 5G towers do not spread coronavirus
outputs.summary: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus and caused an increase in COVID-19 cases is false.
outputs.what_post_claims: The post claims that 5G mobile towers are responsible for spreading the coronavirus, which led to an increase in COVID-19 cases in areas where 5G was installed.
outputs.what_is_true: COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which spreads through respiratory droplets, and there is no scientific evidence linking 5G mobile technology to the spread of the coronavirus, as viruses cannot travel on radio waves.
evidence_against: UN News confirmed in April 2020 that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling it a "hoax that has no technical basis."
Full Fact states that the new coronavirus is a virus and there is no evidence that 5G is harmful to people’s health.
The Washington Post reported that numerous scientific and governmental organizations, including the World Health Organization, have debunked this claim.
outputs.sources_spoken: UN News, Full Fact, and The Washington Post
outputs.audio_script: The post claims that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, causing an increase in COVID-19 cases where 5G was installed. This is false. COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which spreads through respiratory droplets. There is no scientific evidence linking 5G mobile technology to the spread of the coronavirus, as viruses cannot travel on radio waves. We are very sure about this. This information comes from UN News, Full Fact, and The Washington Post.
card_lines: False: 5G towers do not spread coronavirus
Truth: Viruses cannot travel on radio waves
